audience_description: A SaaS growth marketer, product strategist, or founder at a mid-market or enterprise software company who is studying how Hootsuite repositioned upmarket from SMB to enterprise. They want to understand the positioning shift, messaging hierarchy, and go-to-market signals that enabled this transition — so they can either replicate it for their own product or avoid missing similar market opportunities.
recommended_h1_format: How [Company] Repositioned from SMB Scheduler to Enterprise Intelligence Platform: A Homepage Teardown
secondary_keywords: how Hootsuite changed messaging to target enterprise
content_angle: Focus on the POSITIONING ARCHITECTURE, not just visual changes. The searcher needs to understand the deliberate strategic shift from 'time-saving tool for growth' to 'risk mitigation + ROI proof for enterprises.' Show how every element on the page (H1, nav restructure, new feature categories, CTA hierarchy) signals a different buyer persona and buying committee. This is a masterclass in repositioning, not just a design refresh.
what_the_searcher_wants: To see a real, high-performing company execute an upmarket repositioning and understand exactly which messaging, navigation, and CTA changes telegraphed that shift to buyers — so they can apply the same framework to their own product or recognize when a competitor is moving upmarket.
what_to_avoid: Do not treat this as a generic 'before and after' visual comparison or focus on design trends. Avoid missing the BUYER INTENT shift (from individual contributor time-savers to C-suite risk managers). Don't list changes without explaining WHY each change serves the enterprise buyer's job-to-be-done. Don't ignore the removal of SMB-focused messaging ('manage in one place,' customer stories) — these removals are as strategic as the additions.
